set.descent_text: The standard descent reverses the ascent line: back down the summit scrambling, through the upper choss gullies, down the talus to the vine-maple break, and out the 2.7-2.8 miles of trail to the Mineral Creek Trailhead. No rappelling is required on this walk-off/downclimb line (rappels: 0), but the loose upper talus and gullies are generally regarded as more hazardous descending than climbing — face in through the class 3 sections, move deliberately on the small unstable talus, and regroup below rockfall lines rather than descending stacked up. Any snow ramp encountered on the ascent is often the fastest way down (plunge-step or glissade with an axe). Total time from summit to car is commonly reported around 3.5-4 hours. Note: if a party instead climbs the optional South Chimney variant (class 4, on the south face) rather than the standard talus/gully line, that route does NOT walk off — the chimney itself is descended by rappel: two rappels of about 60 ft each, reported consistently in trip logs. Anchors are natural (chockstones, horns, or slung blocks), as this is unbolted alpine rock, so carry cord/webbing to build or back up anchors. A single 60 m rope handles both rappels. Below the chimney, the descent rejoins the same long talus and scree slopes and the trail out. Hazards specific to this variant are loose rock in the chimney and rope-snag risk against the blocky walls.
